name: Food & Nutrition
latestSignal: Food insecurity and malnutrition remain urgent across current public reporting.
mainConstraint: Access, market disruption, supply reliability, and nutrition screening capacity.
now: Prioritize food assistance, nutrition commodities, infant and young child feeding support, and monitoring through responsible channels.
next30Days: Watch acute malnutrition, access interruptions, household coping strategies, and aid pipeline continuity.
next6Months: Sustain nutrition services, local supply restoration, cash or voucher feasibility where appropriate, and safe monitoring systems.
longArc: Rebuild food systems, livelihoods, child nutrition surveillance, and civic trust in equitable assistance.
keyFigures: Acute food insecurity requires continuous review.
Child malnutrition risk remains a priority.
No operational location details are published.
peacebuildingImplications: Food assistance affects dignity, trust, social cohesion, and perceptions of fairness.
Long-term food security connects to livelihoods, governance, and community resilience.

name: Health
latestSignal: Health services remain under severe strain across current public reporting.
mainConstraint: Damaged infrastructure, medicine shortages, access restrictions, fuel dependency, and workforce exhaustion.
now: Support emergency care, essential medicines, referral coordination through established agencies, and protection of health care.
next30Days: Monitor disease outbreaks, trauma care capacity, maternal health, noncommunicable disease continuity, and health worker fatigue.
next6Months: Restore essential services, rehabilitate clinics where feasible, strengthen disease surveillance, and support workforce recovery.
longArc: Rebuild public health systems, mental health capacity, disability support, and institutional trust.
keyFigures: Maternal, trauma, chronic care, and mental health needs intersect.
No facility or route details are published.
peacebuildingImplications: Health repair includes institutional legitimacy, trauma healing, and access fairness.
Protection of health services is central to civilian protection and civic repair.

name: Shelter & Displacement
latestSignal: Shelter needs continue due to displacement and damaged housing.
mainConstraint: Overcrowding, damaged homes, limited materials, access constraints, and winterization risks.
now: Support temporary shelter, household items, safe referrals, and dignified assistance through reviewed organizations.
next30Days: Watch overcrowding, protection risks, weather exposure, and sanitation pressure in displacement settings.
next6Months: Plan repair support, transitional shelter, tenure safeguards, and community-informed reconstruction priorities.
longArc: Housing recovery is also civic repair: property rights, neighborhood reconstruction, memory, and return-related dignity.
keyFigures: Shelter stress increases protection and WASH needs.
peacebuildingImplications: Shelter decisions can reduce or worsen tensions around fairness, identity, and future belonging.
Reconstruction requires rights-aware planning and community participation.

name: Water, Sanitation & Hygiene
latestSignal: WASH risks remain connected to water, sanitation, fuel, and disease prevention.
mainConstraint: Water production, fuel, sewage systems, solid waste, and safe access to hygiene supplies.
now: Support water trucking where appropriate, hygiene kits, sanitation repair, and disease prevention via accountable channels.
next30Days: Watch water quality, diarrheal disease risk, waste accumulation, and fuel-dependent pumping.
next6Months: Repair networks, restore sanitation systems, support community hygiene capacity, and improve monitoring.
longArc: Water governance and equitable services are foundations for dignity, health, and future coexistence.
keyFigures: WASH conditions are linked to disease prevention.
peacebuildingImplications: Shared infrastructure repair can strengthen institutional trust when transparent and inclusive.
WASH access reduces everyday humiliation and protection risk.

name: Education & Children
latestSignal: Education disruption creates immediate and long-term child protection risks.
mainConstraint: Destroyed or inaccessible learning spaces, trauma, family displacement, teacher recovery, and safeguarding needs.
now: Support temporary learning, child protection, psychosocial support, and caregiver-centered services through vetted channels.
next30Days: Watch child protection, family separation risk, learning loss, disability inclusion, and psychosocial distress.
next6Months: Restore learning continuity, teacher support, safe spaces, and structured youth agency under safeguarding protocols.
longArc: Education recovery is trauma repair, civic capacity, memory work, and prevention of future cycles of dehumanization.
keyFigures: Education loss has immediate and generational effects.
Direct unsupervised contact with minors is prohibited.
peacebuildingImplications: Schools can become anchors for psychosocial recovery and plural civic imagination.
Youth agency must be safeguarded, locally led, and non-extractive.

name: Protection, Women, Youth & Social Cohesion
latestSignal: Protection needs are high for women, children, youth, and displaced families.
mainConstraint: Safety risks, displacement stress, gender-based violence risk, psychosocial distress, family separation, and weak referral pathways.
now: Support protection services, psychosocial support, women and youth programming, and safe referral systems through reviewed partners.
next30Days: Watch safeguarding, GBV risk, grief, youth vulnerability, misinformation, and social fragmentation.
next6Months: Strengthen community protection systems, psychosocial care, youth leadership, and trauma-informed civic programs.
longArc: Social cohesion needs justice, acknowledgment, trauma healing, institutional trust, and nonviolent civic capacity.
keyFigures: Protection work requires confidentiality and safeguarding.
Peacebuilding support must avoid manipulation or propaganda.
peacebuildingImplications: Protection and social cohesion connect humanitarian safety with long-term civic repair.
Responsible action must preserve agency and avoid extractive storytelling.
